title: Streaming write-stall + TTL regression — hosted API outage postmortem (2026-04-25)
content:
Summary:

On 2026-04-25 at ~02:12 UTC the hosted streaming API experienced a high-severity outage that manifested as 5xx errors for streaming sessions and extreme tail latency for non-streaming requests. Impact lasted ~43 minutes for customers on affected regions and degraded for another 90 minutes during mitigation rollouts. Root cause: an unintended change to a per-connection TTL/keepalive config combined with an edge buffer write-stall bug in the streaming proxy, which caused head-of-line stalls and backlog amplification under normal traffic spikes.

Impact:
- Scope: ~11% of streaming sessions experienced repeated 5xx (502/504) immediately; additional ~7% of non-streaming requests saw 95th+ latency spikes from 600ms -> 3.2s.
- Customers: 23 enterprise tenants saw visible error rates; a handful of PLG customers reported degraded developer experience. No data loss or model correctness issues were observed.
- Business: Incidents triggered PagerDuty P0 and on-call SREs initiated incident response. External status page was updated.

How it was detected:
- First alert: custom anomaly detector on streaming session error-rate crossed threshold at 02:13 UTC (SRE paging).
- Secondary signals: edge response-time dashboards and increased connection resets observed in edge logs.
- Pager: 02:14 UTC, SRE lead ack at 02:15 UTC.

Timeline (UTC):
- 02:12 — initial spike in streaming session errors; error rate rose from baseline 0.3% to 18% in 2 minutes.
- 02:13 — anomaly alert fires; on-call SRE starts investigation.
- 02:14 — correlating logs show write stall metrics on streaming proxy (high write queue depth).
- 02:18 — quick mitigation: rolling restart of streaming-proxy fleet in affected region, partial drop in errors but tail latency persisted.
- 02:25 — rollback of a recent edge-config change that adjusted connection TTL made at 01:55 UTC. Edge config rollback began.
- 02:35 — error rates fall to ~2%; tail latency trending down but not fully recovered.
- 02:55 — full rollback complete and additional throttling rules temporarily applied; streaming success rates returned to baseline.
- 03:00 — status page updated to reflect mitigation progress.
- 04:30 — follow-up remediation runs and validation; monitoring shows stable behavior. Incident declared mitigated at 04:35.

Root cause analysis (why):
- Primary bug: an existing bug in streaming-proxy write handling where a stalled TCP write (EAGAIN/later drain) could leave per-connection buffers frozen while the proxy's internal queue accounting incorrectly marked the connection as writable. This allowed the proxy to continue accepting streaming state and buffer memory without advancing network writes, producing head-of-line stalls.
- Trigger: a separately deployed edge config tweak at 01:55 UTC reduced keepalive/TTL for upstream connections from 90s -> 10s to aggressively free idle connectors for recent scaling changes. This increased connection churn during normal traffic bursts and surfaced the proxy write-stall bug.
- Amplification: the serving runtime's KV cache prefetch caused more concurrent active streaming sessions per process during a traffic spike at 02:10 UTC, compounding queue depth and memory pressure on streaming-proxy workers.

Contributing factors:
- A config change (edge TTL) was rolled without a targeted canary to measure streaming-specific impact.
- The proxy bug existed in the binary for ~3 months but was low-probability; normal workloads had not triggered it at scale.
- Alerts were configured for absolute error-rate thresholds but not for queue depth or write stall latency in the streaming-proxy.
- Rollback of edge-change required coordination across teams and took longer than expected because the change was bundled with other minor fixes.

Immediate remediation performed:
- 02:18 — rolling restart of streaming-proxy processes to clear stuck write buffers (short-term relief).
- 02:25 — rollback of edge TTL config to previous value (90s).
- 02:55 — deploy temporary traffic shaping: soft concurrency limit per upstream instance and reject-new-session policy for overloaded proxies.

Longer-term fixes and planned actions:
(Planned timeline + owner)
- Fix proxy write-stall bug in runtime and add explicit writeback checks (PR: runtime#657). Owner: Miguel Torres. ETA: 2026-05-03.
- Add unit+integration tests that simulate partial write backpressure and verify buffer accounting. Owner: Juno Kim. ETA: 2026-05-10.
- Update deployment practices: require streaming-sensitive canary (1% traffic for 30m) for edge/TCP-level TTL or connection lifecycle changes. Owner: Priya Raman (edge infra). ETA: 2026-05-01.
- Implement alerting for streaming-proxy write-queue depth and per-connection write latency (new SLI). Owner: Liam O'Connor. ETA: 2026-04-30.
- Run a chaos experiment to model connection churn under reduced TTLs to ensure proxy resilience. Owner: Evelyn Zhang. ETA: 2026-05-07.

Runbook and playbook changes (immediate edits):
- Add a new streaming runbook section: "Detect and mitigate write stalls" including commands for probing write queue depth, safe rolling restart procedure, and temp traffic shaping knobs. Owner: Ana Patel. Actioned: draft added to Confluence, see linked runbook.
- Add step that any edge-level connection/TTL changes must include a streaming-canary approval checkbox. Owner: Priya Raman.

Monitoring & alerts to add/modify:
- New alert: streaming-proxy.write_queue_depth > 500 for > 2m -> P1.
- New alert: streaming-proxy.per_conn_write_latency_p95 > 1s -> P1.
- Adjust anomaly detector to correlate streaming error-rate with write-queue depth before auto-scaling decisions.
- Dashboard: new streaming health panel with per-region metrics: conn churn, write queue depth, buffer memory, and per-second stream accepts.

Customer communication:
- At 02:20 UTC we published a short status page update.
- Post-incident public note to affected tenants drafted and queued for account team review. Owner: Customer Success (cc: Ana Patel). ETA for send: 2026-04-27.

Action items (owner — due):
- Miguel Torres — land runtime fix and coordinate canary release (2026-05-03).
- Juno Kim — add integration tests and run pre-merge CI scenarios (2026-05-10).
- Priya Raman — update edge deployment checklist + canary gating (2026-05-01).
- Liam O'Connor — implement monitoring alerts + dashboard (2026-04-30).
- Evelyn Zhang — run chaos/connection-churn experiment and share findings (2026-05-07).
- Ana Patel — finalize runbook writeup and schedule SRE runbook walk-through (2026-04-29).

Lessons learned / retrospective notes:
- Low-probability bugs can become high-impact when paired with seemingly innocuous config changes (keepalive/TTL tweaks).
- Edge-level changes touching connection lifecycle must be treated as high-risk for streaming customers; they require a streaming-aware canary path.
- Having more fine-grained streaming proxy SLIs (queue depth & per-conn write latency) would have accelerated detection and reduced MTTR.
- Rolling restarts are effective short-term mitigation but we need faster rollback paths for edge configs (decouple TTL change from unrelated cleanup fixes).

Appendix (commands and quick diagnostics):
- Check streaming proxy write queue depth: 
  - curl -s http://proxy-metrics/metrics | grep write_queue_depth | awk '{print $2}'
- Live tail to detect stuck writes: 
  - ssh proxy-node && sudo journalctl -u streaming-proxy -f | grep "write stall"
- Safe rolling restart (recommended): 
  - kubectl rollout restart deployment/streaming-proxy -n hosted-api --selector=region=<region> --max-unavailable=2
